passage:
The school garden had a sign that said, "Do not step on the plants." Still, some students crossed the garden because it was the shortest way to the gym.
The science club made a new sign. It said, "These plants are growing for your lunch next month."
Students stopped walking through the garden.
The club later explained that the vegetables would be used in a cooking class. Once students understood the reason, they cared more.
The first sign gave an order. The second sign gave a connection.
The science teacher said this was a useful lesson. Rules work better when people understand what they protect. A plant is easier to respect when you know it may become your soup.
